title: Native controls vs custom widgets
learningObjectives: Explain native controls vs custom widgets and choose an appropriate native HTML interaction.

understand.concept: Native HTML controls provide built-in semantics, keyboard operation, focus behaviour, and platform integration. Custom widgets may be necessary for specialised interactions, but they must reproduce appropriate roles, states, keyboard patterns, accessible names, and focus management.
understand.whyItMatters: Replacing a native select, checkbox, or disclosure with a custom element creates substantial accessibility and testing work. Prefer native controls unless the requirements genuinely need a custom interaction.
understand.analogy: A native control is a tested tool supplied by the platform; a custom widget means taking responsibility for all the tool's expected behaviour.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual dialog, disclosure, and focus behaviour follows HTML and accessibility platform rules.

explain.narrative: The native select supplies a familiar accessible control. A custom widget would need to recreate selection, keyboard, focus, and form behaviour.

examples.code: The native select already supports keyboard operation and form submission.
examples.explanation: The native select supplies a familiar accessible control. A custom widget would need to recreate selection, keyboard, focus, and form behaviour.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered native disclosure, dialog, or popover example.

practise.guidedTask: Compare a native select with a custom listbox pattern. List the keyboard, focus, ARIA, and form behaviours the custom widget would need.
practise.independentTask: Build an interaction using native HTML first. Test keyboard operation, accessible naming, focus behaviour, and browser support.
hints: Prefer native controls when they meet the requirement.
Give dialogs and popovers clear accessible names and labels.
Test focus entry, dismissal, and return.

questions.prompt: What is the usual preferred starting point for common form controls?
questions.explanation: Native controls provide built-in semantics and interaction behaviour.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between native and custom widgets?
options: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
Whether a custom widget looks more decorative
Whether ARIA can replace all HTML semantics
questions.answer: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
questions.explanation: Native controls are usually the safer choice unless the interaction genuinely requires custom behaviour.
